note.explanation: AI enables computers to perform tasks that usually require human intelligence, while IoT connects physical devices so they can collect and exchange data. Both technologies can improve services and daily life, but they also raise concerns about privacy, security, fairness, jobs and accountability.
note.checkAnswer: IoT connects devices that collect and exchange data.
note.simple: AI helps computers do intelligent tasks. IoT lets connected devices share information. Both can be useful, but people must use them responsibly.
note.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things
steps: AI means machines can perform tasks that normally need human intelligence.
Machine learning uses data so a system can learn patterns and make predictions.
A whitebox model has decisions that people can understand; a blackbox model is difficult to interpret.
IoT devices use sensors, connectivity and data processing to share information and provide services.
Check AI and IoT systems for security, privacy, fairness and effects on people’s work.
note.answer: AI and IoT are technologies that can make services more useful and connected, but they should be developed and used ethically.

mcqs.stem: Q10.1. Which of the following is not a subfield of AI?
rationales: Machine Learning is a subfield of AI.
Natural Language Processing is a subfield of AI.
Computer Vision is a subfield of AI.
Robotics is not listed here as an AI subfield; it is a field that can use AI.

mcqs.stem: Q10.2. Which of these AI algorithms is considered an "explainable" model?
rationales: Neural Networks can be difficult to interpret, so they are often treated as blackbox models.
Decision Trees show decision paths in a form that people can follow.
Random Forests combine many trees, making their overall decisions harder to interpret.
Convolutional Neural Networks can be difficult to interpret, so they are often treated as blackbox models.

mcqs.stem: Q10.3. Which of these is a security concern in IoT deployments?
rationales: Vulnerable devices can be attacked, so this is a concern but not the only one.
IoT data can expose private information, so this is a concern but not the only one.
Lack of standardization can create security weaknesses, so this is a concern but not the only one.
All three listed issues can create security or privacy concerns in IoT deployments.

mcqs.stem: Q10.4. Which of the following is an application of AI in healthcare?
rationales: AI can help personalize drug development, but this is not the only listed application.
AI can support automated diagnosis, but this is not the only listed application.
AI can support remote patient monitoring, but this is not the only listed application.
All three listed activities are applications of AI in healthcare.

mcqs.stem: Q10.5. What is the primary purpose of using AI techniques in machine learning models?
rationales: Improving the accuracy of machine learning models is the primary purpose in this question.
Interpretability can be an important goal, but it is not the primary purpose asked for here.
Reducing computational complexity may be useful, but it is not the primary purpose asked for here.
These are possible aims or benefits, but the question asks for the primary purpose rather than all possible aims.

options: The ability to understand the decision-making process
mcqs.stem:
Q10.6. What is the key difference between explainable (whitebox) and unexplainable
(blackbox) AI models?
rationales: Complexity may affect how easy a model is to explain, but it is not the key difference.
The key difference is whether people can understand how the model makes its decisions.
Performance is not what defines a model as whitebox or blackbox.
Training data can affect a model, but it does not define whether its decisions are understandable.

mcqs.stem: Q10.7. Which of the following is an application of IoT in the transportation domain?
rationales: Connected sensors and systems can support smart traffic management, but this is not the only listed application.
Connected vehicles can exchange information through V2V communication, but this is not the only listed application.
IoT data can help predict when vehicles need maintenance, but this is not the only listed application.
All three listed examples are applications of IoT in transportation.

options: Transformation of job roles and responsibilities
mcqs.stem: Q10.8. What is a potential impact of AI and IoT on the job market?
rationales: Automation can displace some jobs, but this is not the only potential impact.
New technologies can increase demand for specialized skills, but this is not the only potential impact.
Technology can change job roles and responsibilities, but this is not the only potential impact.
All three listed outcomes are potential impacts on the job market.

mcqs.stem:
Q10.9. What is the key concern associated with algorithmic bias in AI-powered
decision-making processes?
rationales: Lack of transparency is a concern in AI, but the key concern associated with bias is that unfair patterns may continue.
Algorithmic bias can perpetuate existing societal biases in decisions, which is the key concern asked about.
Reduced accuracy can be a problem, but it is not the key concern associated specifically with algorithmic bias.
The listed issues are not all the key concern associated specifically with algorithmic bias.

options: Respect for privacy and data rights
mcqs.stem:
Q10.10. Which of the following is an ethical principle that should be considered in the
development and deployment of AI and IoT technologies?
rationales: Transparency and accountability are important principles, but they are not the only ones listed.
Respect for privacy and data rights is important, but it is not the only principle listed.
Fairness and non-discrimination are important, but they are not the only principles listed.
All three listed principles should be considered when developing and deploying AI and IoT.

written.finalAnswer: AI enables machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.

rubric.why: The answer must identify AI as a capability of machines.
rubric.description: Identifies machines performing tasks.
rubric.how: State that machines can perform tasks.

rubric.why: This distinguishes AI tasks from ordinary automated tasks.
rubric.description: Links the tasks to human intelligence.
rubric.how: Explain that these tasks normally require human intelligence.

modelAnswer: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the ability of machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.

written.text: Q10.2. What is the historical context and evolution of AI?
written.finalAnswer: AI developed from early ideas about intelligent machines into modern systems that learn from data and are used in many fields.

rubric.why: This shows awareness of AI's historical beginnings.
rubric.description: Mentions early ideas or development of intelligent machines.
rubric.how: Describe AI as growing from early attempts to make intelligent machines.

rubric.why: This explains how AI has developed into current technology.
rubric.description: Mentions modern learning systems and their use.
rubric.how: State that modern AI learns from data and is used in many fields.

modelAnswer: AI began with early ideas and research into making machines perform intelligent tasks.
It has evolved into modern systems that can learn from data and are used in many fields.

written.text: Q10.3. Provide two examples of AI applications in healthcare.
written.finalAnswer: Automated diagnosis and remote patient monitoring.

rubric.why: One valid healthcare application is required for this mark.
rubric.description: Gives one AI healthcare application.
rubric.how: Name automated diagnosis or personalized drug development.

rubric.why: A second distinct example completes the response.
rubric.description: Gives a second AI healthcare application.
rubric.how: Name another valid application, such as remote patient monitoring.

modelAnswer: Automated diagnosis.
Remote patient monitoring.

written.text: Q10.4. Explain the role of AI techniques in advancing machine learning models.
written.finalAnswer: AI techniques help machine learning models learn patterns from data and improve their performance, including accuracy.

rubric.why: Learning patterns from data is central to machine learning.
rubric.description: Explains how AI techniques help models use data.
rubric.how: State that the techniques let models learn patterns from data.

rubric.why: The answer should state the benefit to the models.
rubric.description: Identifies improved model performance or accuracy.
rubric.how: Explain that learning can improve accuracy or performance.

modelAnswer: AI techniques enable machine learning models to learn patterns from data.
They help improve the performance and accuracy of the models.

written.text: Q10.5. Define the Internet of Things (IoT).
written.finalAnswer: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical devices connected to the internet that collect and exchange data.

rubric.why: A definition must identify IoT as a connected network of things.
rubric.description: Defines IoT as a network of physical or smart devices.
rubric.how: Mention a network of connected devices.

rubric.why: Data collection or exchange describes the purpose of connected IoT devices.
rubric.description: Mentions devices collecting or exchanging data.
rubric.how: State that devices collect and exchange data.

modelAnswer: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical devices connected to the internet.
These devices collect and exchange data.

written.text: Q10.6. Describe the significance of IoT in connecting devices and systems.
written.finalAnswer: IoT connects devices and systems so they can collect, share and use data, enabling communication, monitoring and automation.

rubric.why: The answer must explain that IoT links devices and systems.
rubric.description: Identifies IoT's connecting role.
rubric.how: State that IoT connects devices or systems.

rubric.why: The significance comes from data exchange and the services it enables.
rubric.description: Explains a result of connecting devices.
rubric.how: Mention data sharing, monitoring, communication or automation.

modelAnswer: IoT connects devices and systems so that they can communicate and share data.
This supports monitoring, coordination and automation.

written.text: Q10.7. What are the potential risks associated with AI and IoT?
written.finalAnswer: Potential risks include privacy and security breaches, biased or unfair decisions, job displacement and lack of transparency.

rubric.why: At least one technical or fairness risk must be identified.
rubric.description: Names a privacy, security or bias risk.
rubric.how: Give a relevant risk of AI or IoT.

rubric.why: A second risk demonstrates that the student understands multiple possible harms.
rubric.description: Names another distinct risk.
rubric.how: Add a second relevant risk, such as job displacement.

modelAnswer: AI and IoT can create privacy and security risks, and AI decisions may be biased or difficult to understand.
Automation can also displace some workers.

written.text: Q10.8. Discuss the societal impact of AI and IoT on daily life.
written.finalAnswer: AI and IoT can improve daily services through automation, personalization and connectivity, but can also affect privacy, security and employment.

rubric.why: A complete response should describe a positive effect on everyday life.
rubric.description: Identifies a benefit for society or daily life.
rubric.how: Mention improved services, automation or connectivity.

rubric.why: The impact is balanced by recognizing possible social challenges.
rubric.description: Identifies a possible negative impact.
rubric.how: Mention effects on privacy, security or jobs.

modelAnswer: AI and IoT can make daily services more connected, efficient and personalized.
They can also create concerns about privacy, security and changes to employment.

written.text: Q10.9. Explain the concept of algorithmic bias.
written.finalAnswer: Algorithmic bias occurs when an AI system produces unfair results, often because of biased data or decisions that perpetuate existing societal biases.

rubric.why: The core idea of algorithmic bias is unfairness in outcomes.
rubric.description: Defines bias as unfair system results or decisions.
rubric.how: State that the system produces unfair outcomes.

rubric.why: Explaining a cause or effect shows understanding beyond a bare definition.
rubric.description: Connects bias to data or existing social patterns.
rubric.how: Explain that biased data can reproduce societal bias.

modelAnswer: Algorithmic bias occurs when an AI system produces unfair results or decisions.
It may happen when biased data causes the system to perpetuate existing societal biases.

written.text: Q10.10. Outline the importance of ethical considerations in AI and IoT.
written.finalAnswer: Ethical considerations help ensure that AI and IoT are fair, transparent, accountable and respectful of privacy and data rights.

rubric.why: Ethical principles help guide responsible decisions and technology.
rubric.description: Names a principle for responsible use.
rubric.how: Mention fairness, transparency or accountability.

rubric.why: Protecting people and their information is a central reason for ethics.
rubric.description: Mentions protecting privacy, rights or people from discrimination.
rubric.how: Include respect for privacy and data rights.

modelAnswer: Ethical considerations help make AI and IoT fair, transparent and accountable.
They also protect privacy and data rights and discourage discrimination.

written.text: Q10.1. Discuss the various applications of AI in the field of education. Provide specific examples and explain how AI can enhance the educational experience.
written.finalAnswer: AI can personalize learning, provide intelligent tutoring, automate assessment and support teachers, making education more responsive and accessible.

rubric.why: Personalization is a central educational use of AI.
rubric.description: Explains adaptive or personalized learning.
rubric.how: Describe lessons or content adjusted to student needs and progress.

rubric.why: A specific example shows how students can receive learning support.
rubric.description: Gives an AI tutor or learning assistant example.
rubric.how: Explain how a tutor can give guidance, practice or feedback.

rubric.why: Assessment and feedback are important ways AI can support learning.
rubric.description: Explains automated assessment or feedback.
rubric.how: Give an example of grading, feedback or progress tracking.

rubric.why: The conclusion should explain the overall educational benefit.
rubric.description: Links applications to an improved educational experience.
rubric.how: Explain improved responsiveness, accessibility or teacher support.

modelAnswer: AI can support personalized learning by adapting lessons and practice to each student's needs, pace and progress.
Intelligent tutoring systems can provide explanations, answer questions and give students extra practice.
AI can assess some assignments automatically and provide quick feedback, helping students identify areas for improvement.
Learning systems can track progress and help teachers notice where students need support.
AI tools can also support accessibility, for example by helping provide language or learning assistance.
These applications can make education more responsive and engaging while giving teachers more time to support students.

written.text: Q10.2. Differentiate between explainable (whitebox) and unexplainable (blackbox) AI models.
written.finalAnswer: Whitebox models have decision-making processes that people can understand, while blackbox models produce decisions whose reasoning is difficult to understand.

rubric.why: The defining feature of whitebox AI is understandable reasoning.
rubric.description: Defines explainable or whitebox models.
rubric.how: State that people can understand the model's decision-making process.

rubric.why: The contrast requires an accurate explanation of blackbox models.
rubric.description: Defines unexplainable or blackbox models.
rubric.how: State that their decision-making process is difficult to understand.

rubric.why: The comparison must focus on how decisions are made, not simply model performance.
rubric.description: Makes the key comparison explicit.
rubric.how: Compare the understandability of the models' reasoning.

rubric.why: Examples make the distinction concrete.
rubric.description: Gives suitable examples of model types.
rubric.how: Use a decision tree as an explainable example or a neural network as a commonly blackbox example.

modelAnswer: Explainable, or whitebox, AI models have decision-making processes that people can understand.
A decision tree is an example because its decision path can be followed.
Unexplainable, or blackbox, AI models make decisions whose reasoning is difficult for people to understand.
Neural networks are often treated as blackbox models because their internal reasoning can be difficult to interpret.
The key difference is the ability to understand how the model reaches its decision, not simply its performance.

written.text: Q10.3. Describe the components of an IoT system. Explain how these components work together to enable IoT applications.
written.finalAnswer: An IoT system uses devices and sensors to collect data, connectivity to transmit it, processing to analyse it, and applications or actuators to provide a service or action.

rubric.why: The system needs devices or sensors to gather information from the physical world.
rubric.description: Identifies sensing devices and their role.
rubric.how: Explain that sensors or devices collect data.

rubric.why: Collected data must be communicated between system components.
rubric.description: Identifies connectivity or a network.
rubric.how: Explain how data is sent to other devices or a processing system.

rubric.why: Processing turns collected data into useful information.
rubric.description: Explains data processing or analysis.
rubric.how: Describe analysis by a computer, server or cloud service.

rubric.why: The answer must show how components produce an IoT service or response.
rubric.description: Connects processed data to an application or action.
rubric.how: Explain that an application displays results or a device takes action.

modelAnswer: Sensors and connected devices collect data from the physical environment.
A communication network transfers this data to another device, gateway or processing system.
A computer or cloud service processes and analyses the data.
An application presents useful information to a user or sends a command to a device.
Actuators can carry out a physical action in response to a command.
Together, these components allow an IoT system to sense, communicate, process information and provide a service.

written.text: Q10.4. Explore the applications of IoT in the transportation domain.
written.finalAnswer: IoT supports smart traffic management, Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication and predictive vehicle maintenance.

rubric.why: Traffic management is a key IoT transportation application.
rubric.description: Explains smart traffic management.
rubric.how: Describe connected sensors or systems monitoring traffic and helping manage it.

rubric.why: Vehicle communication is another specific transportation application.
rubric.description: Explains V2V communication.
rubric.how: State that vehicles can exchange information.

rubric.why: The answer should include a further practical use of IoT data.
rubric.description: Explains predictive maintenance.
rubric.how: Describe using sensor data to identify when a vehicle may need maintenance.

rubric.why: An explanation of benefits completes the discussion.
rubric.description: Explains the benefits of the applications.
rubric.how: Link the applications to safety, efficiency or reduced congestion.

modelAnswer: In smart traffic management, connected sensors can collect information about traffic flow and help manage signals or routes.
Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication allows vehicles to exchange information, which can help drivers respond to road conditions.
IoT sensors can monitor the condition of vehicles and support predictive maintenance.
Maintenance can be planned when data indicates a possible problem, rather than waiting for a breakdown.
These applications can improve the efficiency and safety of transportation and help reduce congestion.

written.text: Q10.5. Analyze the potential privacy concerns associated with IoT deployments.
written.finalAnswer: IoT devices may collect sensitive personal data, expose it through weak security or unclear data practices, and allow tracking or unauthorized access; privacy requires data protection, consent and control.

rubric.why: Privacy risks begin with the type and amount of information devices collect.
rubric.description: Identifies the collection of personal or sensitive data.
rubric.how: Explain that connected devices may collect information about people.

rubric.why: The answer must explain how personal information might be exposed or misused.
rubric.description: Identifies a privacy harm or exposure.
rubric.how: Discuss tracking, unauthorized access or breaches.

rubric.why: A reason for the risks is needed to analyse the concern.
rubric.description: Explains a cause of IoT privacy problems.
rubric.how: Mention poor security, unclear data handling or sharing.

rubric.why: Practical protections show how privacy concerns can be addressed.
rubric.description: Suggests privacy safeguards.
rubric.how: Recommend consent, data protection and user control.

modelAnswer: IoT devices may collect large amounts of personal information, such as location, usage patterns or information from connected sensors.
If this data is not protected, it may be exposed through weak device security or unauthorized access.
Data may also be used for tracking or shared in ways users do not expect, especially when data practices are unclear.
Users should be told what information is collected and how it will be used, and their consent should be respected.
IoT systems should protect data and give users suitable control over their information.

written.text: Q10.6. Evaluate the impact of AI and IoT on the job market and work environments.
written.finalAnswer: AI and IoT can automate tasks and change job roles, displacing some workers while increasing demand for specialized skills and creating more connected work environments.

rubric.why: Automation is a major way these technologies affect work.
rubric.description: Explains workplace automation.
rubric.how: Describe tasks or processes that technologies can automate.

rubric.why: Evaluation must acknowledge possible negative employment effects.
rubric.description: Identifies possible job displacement.
rubric.how: Explain that some jobs or tasks may be replaced.

rubric.why: The impact also includes new opportunities and changing skill needs.
rubric.description: Identifies increased demand for skills or new roles.
rubric.how: Mention specialized skills, retraining or new jobs.

rubric.why: The answer should evaluate changes to how work is organized and performed.
rubric.description: Explains changes to work environments or roles.
rubric.how: Describe changing responsibilities or more connected workplaces.

modelAnswer: AI and IoT can automate routine tasks and make work environments more connected and data-driven.
Automation may improve efficiency, but it can also displace workers whose tasks are replaced.
At the same time, demand can grow for specialized skills and workers who can develop, operate or maintain these technologies.
Job roles and responsibilities may change, so workers may need training and opportunities to learn new skills.
Overall, AI and IoT can create benefits and challenges for employment, and their effects depend on how workplaces manage the transition.

written.text: Q10.7. Explain the role of policy and regulatory frameworks in addressing the challenges of AI and IoT. Provide examples of existing frameworks and discuss their effectiveness.
written.finalAnswer: Policies and regulations set rules for privacy, security, fairness and accountability; frameworks such as the EU General Data Protection Regulation and NIST guidance provide useful protections, but effectiveness depends on enforcement and adaptation.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the challenges that policies address.
rubric.description: States what regulation aims to protect or ensure.
rubric.how: Mention privacy, security, fairness or accountability.

rubric.why: The question asks for examples of existing frameworks.
rubric.description: Names a relevant framework or guidance.
rubric.how: Give an example such as the GDPR or NIST guidance.

rubric.why: The student should explain what the example contributes.
rubric.description: Describes the purpose or contribution of a framework.
rubric.how: Explain that it sets expectations or protects data and users.

rubric.why: Evaluation must consider whether frameworks work in practice.
rubric.description: Evaluates effectiveness and limitations.
rubric.how: Explain that effectiveness depends on enforcement, coverage and keeping rules current.

modelAnswer: Policy and regulatory frameworks establish rules and responsibilities for developing and using AI and IoT.
They can address privacy, security, fairness, transparency and accountability.
For example, the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) sets requirements for handling personal data and protecting data rights.
NIST guidance provides recommendations for managing technology-related risks, including cybersecurity risks.
Such frameworks can clarify expectations and encourage organizations to protect people and their information.
Their effectiveness depends on suitable coverage, enforcement and updating the rules as technologies and risks change.

written.text: Q10.8. Describe the concept of algorithmic bias and its implications in AI-powered decision-making processes. Suggest strategies to mitigate the risks of algorithmic bias.
written.finalAnswer: Algorithmic bias occurs when AI decisions produce unfair outcomes and perpetuate societal biases; it can harm individuals and groups, and can be reduced with representative data, testing, transparency, human oversight and accountability.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the unfair results that make an algorithm biased.
rubric.description: Defines algorithmic bias.
rubric.how: State that AI can produce unfair decisions or outcomes.

rubric.why: The answer should explain a cause or social effect of the bias.
rubric.description: Connects bias to data or existing social inequalities.
rubric.how: Explain that biased data can reproduce existing societal biases.

rubric.why: Implications show why algorithmic bias matters.
rubric.description: Explains possible effects on people or decisions.
rubric.how: Describe unfair treatment or discrimination in important decisions.

rubric.why: Mitigation strategies are needed to answer the final part.
rubric.description: Suggests ways to reduce bias.
rubric.how: Recommend representative data, testing, oversight or transparency.

modelAnswer: Algorithmic bias occurs when an AI system produces unfair decisions or outcomes.
It can arise from biased training data or from assumptions in how the system is designed.
The system may then perpetuate existing societal biases in decisions such as selection, access to services or other important areas.
This can unfairly disadvantage individuals or groups and reduce trust in AI systems.
Risks can be reduced by using representative data and checking data and models for unfair patterns.
Systems should be tested regularly, made as transparent as possible and reviewed by people.
Clear accountability is also needed so that problems can be identified and corrected.

written.text: Q10.9. Develop a set of ethical principles and guidelines for the responsible development and deployment of AI and IoT technologies.
written.finalAnswer: Responsible AI and IoT should follow fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, security, human oversight and respect for data rights throughout development and deployment.

rubric.why: Fair treatment is a fundamental ethical principle.
rubric.description: Includes fairness and non-discrimination.
rubric.how: Require systems to avoid unfair treatment of individuals or groups.

rubric.why: People should be able to question decisions and responsibility should be clear.
rubric.description: Includes transparency or accountability.
rubric.how: Require clear decision processes and responsible oversight.

rubric.why: AI and IoT systems must protect personal data and connected devices.
rubric.description: Includes privacy, data rights or security.
rubric.how: Set rules for consent, data protection and security.

rubric.why: Practical guidelines make principles part of design and use.
rubric.description: Includes a guideline for responsible implementation.
rubric.how: Require human review and ongoing checks during development and deployment.

modelAnswer: AI and IoT systems should be fair and should not discriminate against individuals or groups.
Their design and decisions should be as transparent as possible, and organizations should be accountable for their effects.
Systems should respect privacy and data rights by collecting only appropriate data and protecting it from unauthorized access.
Security should be considered throughout development and deployment, including for connected devices.
People should have suitable human oversight and a way to raise concerns about important decisions.
Systems should be tested and monitored after deployment so that errors, unfair outcomes and security problems can be corrected.
These guidelines help ensure responsible development and use of AI and IoT technologies.

examTips: Section A tests definitions, examples and the key differences between AI and IoT concepts. Read every option carefully, especially options ending in “All of the above.”
Short questions are commonly worth 2 marks: give a direct definition or two distinct points, and include a relevant example when asked.
For long questions, organize the answer into clear points. Define the concept, describe applications or risks, and explain their effects or solutions.
For compare questions, state the difference directly and include an example of each type where useful.
For ethical or policy questions, name principles or frameworks and explain how they protect people; also mention limitations such as enforcement.

explain.title: Artificial Intelligence
explain.body: AI enables machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence. Machine learning is an AI approach in which systems learn patterns from data. AI is used in fields such as healthcare and education.

explain.title: Explainable and unexplainable AI
explain.body: Whitebox models have decision-making processes that people can understand; decision trees are an example. Blackbox models are difficult to interpret; neural networks are often treated as blackbox models.

explain.title: Internet of Things
explain.body: IoT connects physical devices and systems so they can collect, exchange and use data. Sensors gather information, networks transfer it, and processing systems or applications use it to provide a service or action.

explain.title: Benefits and risks
explain.body: AI and IoT can improve services, support monitoring and automation, and change transport, education and healthcare. Risks include privacy and security problems, unfair decisions, job displacement and lack of transparency.

explain.title: Responsible technology
explain.body: Responsible AI and IoT should be fair, transparent and accountable, protect privacy and data rights, and include security and human oversight. Representative data and regular checks can help reduce algorithmic bias.

mistakes: Do not confuse a model’s accuracy with whether people can understand its decision-making process.
When defining IoT, mention connected devices and their collection or exchange of data.
Do not describe algorithmic bias only as low accuracy; explain that it can produce unfair decisions and perpetuate societal biases.
For long questions, avoid listing examples without explaining how they work or why they matter.
When discussing AI and IoT risks, include both technical risks, such as security and privacy, and social effects, such as fairness and employment.
